chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from al-Ala' ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The Honour is the Gown of Allah, and the Pride is His Garment. So whoever holds onto any of these, Allah will cast him into Hell.'

key_terms.الْكِبْرُ: Pride, majesty, or greatness (divine attribute, distinct from human arrogance)
key_terms.رِدَاءُ اللَّهِ: The Gown of Allah (metaphor for divine attribute)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'The Honour is the Gown of Allah' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) identifies 'al-'Izz' (Honour/Majesty) and 'al-Kibr' (Pride) as the exclusive garments of Allah, using the metaphor of a cloak and waist-wrapper to signify divine sovereignty. This teaching is central to Shia theology regarding 'Tajalli al-Sifat' (manifestation of attributes), warning that human arrogance constitutes a usurpation of divine prerogatives, thereby warranting the punishment of being cast into Hellfire.
